entries.clue: Advantage of computerised identikit picture when pursuing crook virtually (7)

blocks.note: a crook is BENT; 'virtually' (= almost) stops it one letter short
an E-fit is the digital identikit UK police issue

annotation.walkthrough: 'Virtually' means almost, and it is doing surgery rather than describing: it docks the final letter. An E-fit is the digital identikit UK police issue, hidden here behind ordinary-sounding police work.
annotation.definitionFit: A benefit is an advantage — the sense in 'the benefits of exercise' — a plain synonym while the surface suggests welfare payments.

entries.clue: On vacation Bradley Walsh ultimately ignored resort’s in-house rules? (6)

blocks.note: 'on vacation' vacates the word, keeping only B(radle)Y
'ultimately ignored' drops the last letter; 'resort' then re-sorts WALS into LAWS

annotation.walkthrough: Bradley Walsh of The Chase is pure misdirection. 'On vacation' vacates a word — only the outside letters stay — and 'resort' quietly re-sorts what is left of Walsh.
annotation.definitionFit: By-laws are the local rules a council or club sets for its own patch — exactly what a resort would post as in-house rules.

entries.clue: Finally – given you identified graffiti artist – Banksy’s in exposed state (6)

blocks.clueFragment: given you identified graffiti artist – Banksy
blocks.note: the final letters of each of the six words

annotation.walkthrough: 'Finally' governs all six words at once — each donates its last letter. The dashes fence the fodder off from the definition at the end.
annotation.definitionFit: Nudity is the state of being exposed — undressed — and the clue winks at Banksy's hidden identity finally being exposed too.

entries.clue: In France and in Germany, shaver sounded 1 across? (4-6)

blocks.note: F is the international vehicle code for France

annotation.walkthrough: Two languages in one charade: France's international car-sticker F, then 'and' as a German would say it. Say RAISER aloud and the shaver appears.
annotation.definitionFit: A fund-raiser and a benefit are the same event — a show staged to raise money — so the answer defines 1 across, BENEFIT.

entries.clue: Tax article without it (5)

annotation.walkthrough: 'Without' wears its old meaning of 'outside': THE stands without IT rather than lacking it. Three tiny words, one neat trap.
annotation.definitionFit: A tithe was the tenth of one's produce owed to the church — a levy, so 'tax' is a plain synonym.

entries.clue: Spotted predator – shark is caught (7)

annotation.walkthrough: 'Caught' means caught by the ear. The shark plays cards — a cheater — and saying it aloud releases the big cat.
annotation.definitionFit: A cheetah is a spotted big cat that hunts — literally a predator with spots — while 'spotted' pretends to mean 'seen'.

entries.clue: My friend entertains men with essentially new material (9)

annotation.walkthrough: COR and 'my!' are both exclamations of surprise, and OR is the army's 'other ranks' — two conventions worth banking. PAL swallows them both.
annotation.definitionFit: Corporeal means bodily — 'material' in the philosopher's sense of having physical substance, the opposite of spiritual.

entries.clue: Ages in prison’s manure shed (4)

blocks.note: a dungeon is a prison; the possessive S stays on
shed from the front of DUNGEONS

annotation.walkthrough: The prison is a DUNGEON — keep its possessive S — and shedding the manure from its front leaves the answer. No outbuilding involved.
annotation.definitionFit: Eons are vast stretches of geological time — 'ages' in the everyday sense of 'it took ages', and both are plurals.

entries.clue: A film star cycles and waves (8)

blocks.note: a film over the eyes is a mist

annotation.walkthrough: Cycling moves letters round without changing their order — the tail comes to the front, like cutting a deck of cards. It is rarer than a reversal and easy to miss, and 'cycles' is its usual signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Tsunamis are enormous sea waves — a plain plural-for-plural definition hiding at the end of a chatty surface.

entries.clue: Pine nut’s beginning to be problem (8)

blocks.note: slang for the head; it begins the answer

annotation.walkthrough: The order is the trick: 'nut's beginning' announces that HEAD starts the answer, so the ACHE clued first goes second.
annotation.definitionFit: A headache is figuratively any nagging problem — 'this rota is a real headache' — not just the pain itself.

entries.clue: Young male nurse is loaded (5)

annotation.walkthrough: 'Young male nurse' begs to be read as one job title — resist. EN, the old Enrolled Nurse grade, is a crossword regular.
annotation.definitionFit: Laden means loaded — both past participles, a lorry laden or loaded with cargo — while the surface hints at 'loaded' meaning rich.

entries.clue: Tea, cream – not full fat – oddly it’s a Cambodian delicacy (9)

blocks.note: its odd letters — first, third, fifth and so on, punctuation ignored

annotation.walkthrough: Run through 'Tea, cream – not full fat' and take every odd-numbered letter, punctuation ignored. Fried tarantula genuinely is Cambodian street food.
annotation.definitionFit: Fried tarantula, a-ping, is a real delicacy in Cambodia, so the definition is a literal dish, not a description of the spider.

entries.clue: Call Musk with Washington opening that ought to bear fruit (10)

blocks.note: the state's postal code; 'opening' sends it to the front
to call something is to term it
first name of the Tesla owner

annotation.walkthrough: WA is clued last but 'opening' promotes it to the front of the answer. The Musk-in-Washington surface is pure news-cycle noise.
annotation.definitionFit: A watermelon is simply a fruit — definition by broad category, the fairest kind — while the surface chases tech billionaires.

entries.clue: Two Americans holding back on driving range (3)

blocks.note: A = American, twice — one either side

annotation.walkthrough: 'Driving range' wants to be golf — split it. An Aga is the great British kitchen range, and A for American serves twice.
annotation.definitionFit: An Aga is the classic cast-iron cooking range — 'range' as kitchen stove, not golf practice or open country.

entries.clue: School paid to spin results in mock (10)

blocks.note: anagram fodder — ten letters, schooled into shape

annotation.walkthrough: 'School' is the anagram indicator: schooling knocks raw material into shape. 'Mock' defines the answer in its old sense of deceiving hopes.
annotation.definitionFit: To mock hopes is to disappoint them — the older sense in which fate mocks our plans, deceiving rather than ridiculing.

entries.clue: Pop singer’s ill – lie about swallowing pill in trashed Ibis hotel (6,6)

annotation.walkthrough: Everything goes in one pot: ILL, LIE, an E — the clubber's pill — and IBIS with hotel's phonetic H. The trashed-hotel surface suits the pop-star story.
annotation.definitionFit: Billie Eilish is the American pop star behind 'Bad Guy' — a name-the-person definition rather than a synonym.

entries.clue: Conducted lessons in English, with students covering tenses – one might appear with a smile (5,4)

definitions.text: one might appear with a smile

blocks.note: to conduct lessons is to teach
T = tense; both Ts of TAUGHT-IN-E get covered

annotation.walkthrough: 'Covering' as in covering someone's shift: the student Ls stand in for the two tense Ts of TAUGHT IN E, and the wrinkle appears.
annotation.definitionFit: A laugh line is both a scripted joke meant to raise a smile and the wrinkle smiling leaves by your eyes — the definition covers either sense.

entries.clue: Leaves power drills on the counter, securely fastened (8)

annotation.walkthrough: P for power 'drills' into DEPARTS, and 'on the counter' — running against the flow — turns the whole assembly around.
annotation.definitionFit: Strapped means fastened down with straps, hence securely fastened — while the surface nudges you towards strapped for cash.

entries.clue: Sedative not applicable on piercing in the middle of the ear (8)

annotation.walkthrough: PIERCING surrenders its exact centre, and OTIC — 'of the ear' — turns an ear-piercing surface into anatomy.
annotation.definitionFit: A narcotic is a drug that dulls the senses and brings on sleep — a sedative by definition, noun for noun.

entries.clue: TV star barking cruelly at crew (6.6)

blocks.note: to crew a ship is to man it

annotation.walkthrough: 'Barking', as in barking mad, does the mixing — but 'crew' must first become MAN, to crew a ship being to man it. One synonym step hides inside the anagram.
annotation.definitionFit: Tracey Ullman is the comedian whose sketch shows ran on both British and American television — a straight name-the-celebrity definition.

entries.clue: Stock of wine merchant delivered (6)

annotation.walkthrough: 'Delivered' means spoken, as a line is delivered — so it is the wine merchant's homophone that goes in the grid, not the merchant.
annotation.definitionFit: A collector's cellar means the bottles themselves — 'a fine cellar' is a stock of wine, not the room it sits in.

entries.clue: Gossipy magazine journalist is excited (6)

annotation.walkthrough: Heat is Britain's celebrity-gossip weekly and ED crosswordland's hardest-working journalist. Two conventions, one join.
annotation.definitionFit: A heated exchange is an excited, worked-up one — both words describe tempers rather than temperature.

entries.clue: Bow and scrape while retreating to some extent (3)

annotation.walkthrough: 'Bow and scrape' reads as one grovelling idiom, but only 'scrape' carries the answer — read it in retreat. 'To some extent' is the classic hidden-word flag.
annotation.definitionFit: An arc is a bow in the curve sense — an archer's bow or a rainbow's bend — not the polite bending the idiom suggests.

entries.clue: Hunk needing reason to start op-ed? (5,5)

blocks.note: 'to start' sends it to the front
a hunk of bread is a piece

annotation.walkthrough: Like 8 down, the charade arrives out of order: 'to start' sends the reason to the front of the hunk.
annotation.definitionFit: A think piece is a reflective opinion article — just what runs as an op-ed — and the question mark admits the equivalence is loose.

entries.clue: Lowest point of brain drain with regular emigration climbing (5)

blocks.note: what remains — b(R)a(I)n(D)r(A)i(N) — once every other letter emigrates

annotation.walkthrough: 'Regular emigration' is the joke: every other letter of BRAIN DRAIN emigrates, and what stays behind climbs the down entry.
annotation.definitionFit: The nadir is the spot directly beneath an observer — the zenith's opposite — hence the lowest point of fortunes as well as skies.

entries.clue: Excellent, for example, to be Morocco-bound (4)

blocks.note: the international vehicle code; it does the binding

annotation.walkthrough: 'Morocco-bound' looks like travel but means bound in morocco, the goatskin leather of fine bookbinding — so Morocco's car-code MA wraps the example.
annotation.definitionFit: Mega is slang promoted to adjective: 'that gig was mega' means excellent; the Greek prefix just means huge.

entries.clue: Corrupt state maybe does if cutting back (9)

blocks.note: to state a case is to put it
does are deer — 'maybe' flags the definition by example
cuts into DEER before everything reverses

annotation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' flags does as one example of DEER. IF cuts in, the whole DEIFER assembly reverses, and PUT — to state a case is to put it — leads off.
annotation.definitionFit: Putrefied flesh is corrupt in the word's oldest sense — rotted, decayed — not the bribery the surface implies.

entries.clue: Initially in sonatas, Liszt enjoyed this minor key (5)

blocks.note: the first letters of the five words

annotation.walkthrough: 'Initially' harvests the first letters of five words. The definition is the delight: a key, as in the Florida Keys, is a small island, so a minor key is no music at all.
annotation.definitionFit: An islet is a little island, and a key — as in the Florida Keys — is a small island too, so a minor key is an islet.

entries.clue: Expensive – taking 150 Euros, say (7)

blocks.note: E for euro, closing the word

annotation.walkthrough: The throwaway 'say' is the definition — to say is to declare. DEAR takes Roman-numeral CL, and the euro's single E closes the word.
annotation.definitionFit: To declare is simply to say — 'she declared her innocence' — though customs desks make the word feel weightier.

entries.clue: In bed, weary, drinking wine – quite the opposite (7)

blocks.note: as a verb — to weary is to tire
it ends up doing the drinking

annotation.walkthrough: 'Quite the opposite' is an instruction, not a comment: it inverts the container the clue has just described, so the drinker becomes the drunk. The clue and its answer describe the same sleepy evening.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone who has retired for the night is in bed — the verb's going-to-bed sense rather than the pensioner's.
